question: Question linked to the image nº24 Brain CT scan performed as a matter of urgency in the case of cranioencephalic traumatism. What is your diagnosis?:
analysis: In cases of cranioencephalic trauma, the CT scan findings are crucial for diagnosis. An acute subdural hematoma typically presents as a crescent-shaped hyperdense area on the CT, often associated with underlying brain injury. An epidural hematoma usually appears as a biconvex shape and is often linked to skull fractures. Cortical injury or cerebral contusion would show localized areas of edema or hemorrhage in the brain tissue. Intraventricular hemorrhage is characterized by blood within the ventricular system. Without the image, the most common acute finding in trauma is an acute subdural hematoma, especially if there is a history of rapid deceleration or impact.
